Ribston Hall High School
Here at Ribston Hall High School we’re a community. A community of creative thinkers, top performers and future leaders. Of happy, ambitious people.
Pupils relish learning and thrive on the challenge presented by difficult concepts in lessons. Staff know pupils well. They share warm relationships. This detailed knowledge and trust enable pupils to consistently achieve above national averages in national examinations.
Joining Ribston in Year 7 was a great experience. I felt welcomed straight away thanks to the summer school and induction days, which helped me make friends and feel more confident before lessons even began. The teachers are kind and always take time to explain things to you if you need help, so you really feel you’re encouraged in all your subjects. The school is also really inclusive - everyone’s encouraged to be themselves, and we have lots of clubs to choose from across things like music, sports, and drama. I would definitely recommend coming to Ribston - it has so many opportunities and really helps you be the best you can be.
I thoroughly enjoyed my experiences at school. Both the academic and creative sides of me were nurtured at Ribston, which ultimately led me to my career choice as a barrister. I was heavily involved in music, and Ribston gave me opportunities to lead, to take part in public speaking, and organise charity events - all of which built my confidence and my drive to help others. The teachers really cared about our development as individuals and encouraged us to be independent, so I’m grateful to them. The ethos of the school is to create well-rounded individuals, and my time there was fundamental to the person I went on to become.
Satya Talwar Mouland, Barrister (Ribston Alumna 2004 - 2011)
Ribston offers fantastic leadership and career development opportunities. Since joining as Curriculum Lead for Modern Foreign Languages, I have been supported by the senior team in expanding my coaching skills, both formally and informally, which has helped me to lead the MFL team. I have been given numerous opportunities to develop and support other staff across the school, and I feel fully supported myself. Most importantly, the students are a joy to teach; they're articulate, confident, and happy, which makes it very enriching to be a teacher at Ribston.
ELISHMA LAWLESS, CURRICULUM LEAD FOR MFL

Shaping Futures Programme
At Ribston, we want every child in our local area to have a fair chance to join our school and feel part of our community. We are part of the 'Shaping Futures' initiative which was set up by Pate's Grammar School and is a partnership project with the other grammar schools in Gloucestershire.
Our aim is to encourage equal opportunity regardless of a child's background and by widening access to grammar school for Pupil Premium and Pupil Premium Plus children. We do this by identifying and removing barriers there may for local families and providing support and resources that they can easily access.
We partner with primary schools in our local area, and both our teachers and students get involved in activities with children and teachers from these schools throughout the year – from computers to drama, cooking and sport. We are partnered with 13 schools and are delighted to offer our current programmes of activity to:
Calton Primary School
Finlay Community School
Linden Primary School
St Pauls CofE Primary School and Nursery
St James' CofE Primary School (Gloucester)
Heron Primary School
Upton St Leonards CofE Primary School
Meadowside Primary School
Waterwells Primary Academy
Tredworth Junior School
Hillside Primary School
Widden Primary School
Removing barriers to access
The Shaping Futures Programme begins when Head Teachers' from our Primary Partnership schools nominate high-attaining Pupil Premium students. After this, we are in contact with families who can register on the programme and families then start their journey with us. This includes:
If your child has been eligible for free school meals at any point in the last six years, please register via the following link: Atom Learning: Ribston Hall High School Registration. You will be given free access to Atom Home when your child’s Pupil Premium status has been verified by their primary school.
Pupil Premium information
Further information about Pupil Premium can be found on our Inclusion page and Statutory Information page. For more information on its purpose, how the School uses the grant, eligibility, funding allocation information and how to request support, please read our Pupil Premium Policy and Statement on our Policies Page.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ribston Hall High School - "Positive change" to admissions test arrangements for grammar schools in Gloucestershire announced
pageCache.text:
"Positive change" to admissions test arrangements for grammar schools in Gloucestershire announced
The seven Gloucestershire Grammar Schools (G7) have appointed Future Stories Community Enterprise (FSCE) as their new admissions test provider for entry to Year 7 from 2028 onwards, following a comprehensive competitive tender process.
The procurement sought an organisation with proven technical expertise, robust security, strong capacity for large‑scale assessment, and a commitment to fair and accessible selective testing. FSCE was selected from a field of qualified national providers.
A New Chapter for Grammar School Admissions in Gloucestershire
Each year, around 3,000 children register to sit the Gloucestershire Grammar Schools admissions test, with approximately 2,500 taking part. The G7 schools operate a shared testing process, enabling families to sit one test for entry to all seven schools.
As part of the new arrangements, the Gloucestershire Grammar Schools have also taken the decision to move the test date from September of Year 6 to the latter part of the summer term of Year 5. This will reduce pressure on pupils beginning Year 6 and provide families with earlier results. These arrangements will take effect from summer 2027 for first entry into Year 7 in September 2028.
Under the new arrangements, FSCE will design, develop, and deliver the test papers – including scoring, analysis, age‑standardisation, and secure reporting of results – and will provide specialist guidance and support to admissions teams across all seven schools.
FSCE, a not‑for‑profit subsidiary of Reading School, develops bespoke admissions assessments designed specifically for selective state grammar schools. Their tests are currently used by twelve grammar schools and consortia nationally, with more than 8,000 pupils sitting FSCE papers each year.
The G7’s decision reflects FSCE’s strong technical expertise in designing valid, curriculum‑aligned assessments; its commitment to fairness and accessibility through inclusive design and its shared focus on widening access for disadvantaged pupils.
A Focus on Fairness and Opportunity
A key objective of the G7 tender was to identify an assessment provider whose tests support fair access for all pupils, regardless of background. FSCE’s approach draws heavily on Key Stage 2 curriculum content, ensuring accessibility for children from a wide range of primary schools and reducing reliance on specialist 11+ tutoring. FSCE also provides adapted formats - including Braille, large print and modified papers - and expert support for schools making reasonable adjustments for candidates with additional needs.
A spokesperson for Future Stories Community Enterprise (FSCE) said:
“We are delighted to be working with the Gloucestershire Grammar Schools, who share our vision for fairer selective admissions. At the heart of our approach is a commitment to ensuring that assessments identify true potential, not just prior advantage.
Through research and data-led test design, we aim to dissuade intensive test preparation and encourage natural curiosity and critical thinking. We focus on creating accessible and inclusive tests that maintain the highest standards of rigorous selective assessment and demystifying admissions processes through cohesive partnerships with schools, children and their families.
Working in unison with all schools in the G7, we look forward to developing robust, fair and innovative assessments, to build on the success of the Shaping Futures outreach work and to continue widening participation so that every child has an equal opportunity to demonstrate their ability.”
Alec Waters, Headteacher of Ribston Hall High School said:
“The appointment of FSCE marks an important step forward for grammar school admissions in Gloucestershire. Their strong alignment with the Key Stage 2 curriculum, combined with a clear commitment to fairness, accessibility and high‑quality assessment, gives us confidence that the test will identify genuine academic potential.
Moving the test to the summer term of Year 5 is also a positive change for children and families, reducing pressure at the start of Year 6 and avoiding the potential learning gap of the summer holiday. As part of the G7, we are committed to ensuring that selective education remains ambitious, rigorous and as fair as possible for all pupils.”
Over the coming months, FSCE and G7 admissions teams will work closely together on:
Further details will be available on each school’s website at the start of the next academic year (September 2026).
If you have any questions about the new arrangements, please contact Mrs Denice Murphy (Admissions Manager for Ribston Hall High School) via email: admissions@ribstonhall.gloucs.sch.uk.

pageCache.text:
Writing my way to victory: my journey from pen to prize
No child deserves to grow up without a childhood as we understand childhood. That right to play, that right to learn, that right to share without being afraid
On Thursday 12th June, I was honoured to have been invited to attend the Dulverton Essay Prize Evening at King’s School. The theme for this year’s 1,500-word essay was inspired by one of War Photographer Adam Dobby’s photographs entitled: “Hope: the stubborn, the unconquerable," with the accompanying quote: “No child deserves to grow up without a childhood as we understand childhood. That right to play, that right to learn, that right to share without being afraid …”
Adam Dobby is a former SAS staff sergeant turned award-winning war photographer, known for his motto “I put down my rifle and picked up a camera,” reflecting his mission to capture human stories from conflict zones with compassion and honesty.
In response to my entry being highly commended by the judges (including Headmaster Mr David CA Morton, Dr Matthew Lim, Mr Tom Horler-Underwood, and Adam Dobby himself), I was honoured to be shortlisted as a finalist!
The entries were judged on Originality, Academic Rigour and Relevance to the title; the best two essays from Key Stage 4 and 5 were shortlisted and invited to an evening with Adam Dobby.
My winning essay, entitled: “Stolen Childhoods: Reclaiming the Right to Dream,” explored the harsh realities faced by children living in conflict and poverty across the globe. Drawing from the theme of hope combined with the perspicuous and representative adjective, ‘unconquerable’ - with connotations of being impossible to obtain for deprived, marginalised children all over the world - I crafted the refrain: “Hope is not a luxury. Hope is a lifeline. Hope is a right.” My essay interweaves real-life global examples with a descriptive, story-like tone: illustrating my unique writing style, and aiming to evoke empathy; advocating for awareness to the everyday struggles of forgotten children.
My family and I had the pleasure of attending the Awards Ceremony along with the other finalists; I was delighted to be announced as the overall winner of the Dulverton Essay Competition 2025—an unforgettable moment that filled me with pride! This was an incredible achievement for which I am deeply appreciative and proud to have received such meaningful recognition, reflecting both my passion for writing and the hard work I put into my entry.
As part of the award, I received a £100 Waterstones gift voucher and a signed copy of Adam Dobby’s photograph: Hope: the stubborn, the unconquerable — a meaningful and lasting reminder of the experience.
Dr Matthew Lim from King’s School described the Awards Evening as extraordinary and awe-inspiring, saying:
Each pupil who gave us a short summary of their writing and engaged with Adam – he gave first-hand accounts of his experience in conflict-zones. The evening saw us use each pupils' essay as a springboard for deep conversations with Adam which were stimulating, thought-provoking and filled with empathy, compassion and humanity.
Winning this competition has not only given me confidence in my voice as a writer, but also encouraged me to keep exploring ideas that matter. As I look ahead, I hope to continue using words to make a meaningful impact — and to stand up for those whose stories too often go unheard.

Careers Advice and Guidance
At Ribston Hall High School, we are committed to helping every student discover their strengths, explore future possibilities and make informed decisions about their next steps. Careers education is woven throughout our curriculum and wider school experience, ensuring students develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to succeed in an ever-changing world.
Careers guidance is tailored to pupils' aspirations. The school engages well with employers. Pupils have an informed understanding of how to achieve their ambitions. Equipped with this knowledge, sixth-form students and pupils are well positioned to pursue their chosen next steps.
From Year 7 through to Sixth Form, our students benefit from a comprehensive careers programme that includes employer encounters, workplace experiences, higher education guidance, apprenticeship information, careers fairs and personalised support. Through these opportunities, students gain valuable insight into the wide range of pathways available to them and are empowered to pursue ambitions that reflect their individual talents and interests.
Whether a student's aspirations lie in university, degree apprenticeships, employment, entrepreneurship or specialised training, our aim is to help them develop the confidence and skills needed to thrive. Guided by our values of being ambitious academic learners, confident and creative thinkers, and proud members of the Ribston community, we support every student to look beyond the classroom and prepare for life beyond school.
Careers Education at Ribston
Preparing students for the future is about more than academic success. Our careers programme helps students:
We believe every student should leave Ribston equipped with the knowledge, experiences and aspirations needed to achieve their personal goals.
Our careers programme supports students throughout their educational journey, helping them understand how their interests, talents and academic achievements can lead to exciting opportunities in the future.

All students have access to Unifrog, a careers package full of advice, opportunities and information. Unifrog allows students to explore their personal skills, qualities and interests. It has tools to help students source opportunities at universities in the UK, US and European as well as apprenticeships. They are also able to access a full careers library, online webinars and open learning courses to enhance their careers research. We use the Unifrog placement tool to support students organising their own work experience in Year 12. It can be accessed from the student dashboard.

Sixth Form Careers Advice and UCAS Information
We recognise careers guidance and advice is key to ensuring all students are fully informed of the range of career opportunities and pathways available to them. They are encouraged to raise their aspirations, supported to explore all options and, critically, they are empowered to make positive decisions which enable them to manage their own career development effectively and confidently.
Careers forms part of the PHSE curriculum, during which we deliver a range of practical enterprise and employability activities to equip students with the knowledge and skills to understand and capitalise on the opportunities presented to them.
We have a series of focused Careers and PHSE days throughout the year when we invite outside organisations to school to run sessions with the students. During recent Careers and PHSE days, we have hosted interactive sessions with Barclays Lifeskills, Gloucestershire Police and the University of Gloucestershire.
We work with Gloucestershire Careers Hub. This is a resource for people at any stage in their career, including links to support and helpful organisations. The Gloucestershire Careers and Skills Portal provides free resources to improve careers education and skills across the county.
Our Careers programme starts with our youngest students. However, it accelerates for our Sixth Form students as they approach the end of their formal school education. We aim to meet the individual needs of students by providing encounters with employers and Further/Higher Education providers, workplace insights, curriculum-linked careers information and resources, and impartial bespoke guidance. Our sixth form careers provision is summarised here:
Extended careers appointments Each student is entitled to as many one-hour appointments with our Careers Adviser as they need. These appointments are to discuss next steps in terms of education, job opportunities, apprenticeship roles, training, voluntary work and work experience. Students are encouraged to apply for subject taster days, summer schools and workshops to build their insight and support their development.
Help with UCAS applications Following a Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (UCAS) introductory session in Year 11, a Year 12 group session for all registering students explores the process in greater depth, which is followed by ongoing support to complete UCAS applications, including Personal Statement compilation. We invite speakers into school from universities to help with raising aspirations and informing students of the practical aspects of Higher Education, such as student finance. The School Liaison Officer for Robinson College, University of Cambridge, came into school recently to talk to our students about applying to competitive university courses, offering hints and tips on achieving a candidate interview.
Support to find work experience placements We encourage all Year 12 students to partake in work experience placements; we offer assistance with finding and making contact with companies. In addition to sharing opportunities at Primary Schools within our local Shaping Futures Programme, we signpost all opportunities with local organisations to our students to enable them to capitalise on work experience opportunities.
Careers Conversations These careers sessions run regularly in the library. They are open to all years but are particularly relevant to our Sixth Form students who may already have taken the first steps towards a specific career path with their Sixth Form choices. They usually take the form of visitors talking about their role and career path, as well as answering questions from students on industry and role specifics, however we have also enjoyed many online lectures during the pandemic. We enjoy hosting speakers, particularly former students, to give industry insights and specific career advice.
Subject Specific Events Individual departments hold career-specific sessions with relevant activities and speakers, such as a Criminology day, a physical theatre workshop or a session on designing computer games.
Trips and visits As well as group attendance at university open days, we visit careers fairs and UCAS events. We’ve previously visited the University of Bath, Oxford University, and careers fairs in Bristol and Birmingham. These visits offer insights for apprenticeships as well as Higher Education, so they cater for the next steps of most students. Our Enrichment programme also delivers in-depth learning opportunities for students to help them in their future career, such as Geography trips to Iceland and Naples, or Modern Foreign Language (MFL) trips to France or Spain.
Promotion of learning and development opportunities In addition to sharing work experience opportunities with students, we publicise online lectures, apprenticeships, Open days and Massive Open Online Courses (MOOC) such as IBM’s ‘Analysing Data with Excel’ or ‘Science Writing’ from the University of Leeds. Future Learn is a valuable resource, bringing together opportunities for extra-curricular learning from some of the world’s top universities and employers. We offer multiple clubs and other development and leadership opportunities which may benefit students in their future career choices, such as Medical Society, Dissection Club, Feminism Society, and roles such as Peer Mentor, House Captain, Subject Lead and becoming part of the Head Student team.
Our Career provision delivers more than advice about university courses; we work with students to explore options for those students who don’t feel university is right for them. Undertaking voluntary work abroad, embarking on an apprenticeship or direct entry to employment may be the appropriate next step for some students.
We consider the needs of all students with our Careers programme, occasionally considering specialist provision, training courses or volunteering opportunities for students with SEN or additional needs.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ribston Hall High School - Celebrating GCSE Success on Results Day
pageCache.text:
Celebrating GCSE Success on Results Day
There were smiles, celebrations and plenty of proud moments as Ribston students and their families joined us today to collect their GCSE results.
We were delighted to welcome students and parents into school to share in this important milestone, celebrating the hard work, commitment and determination that have led to today’s achievements.
Our staff team were on hand throughout the morning to congratulate students, offer guidance and help them plan their next steps for the future. We are especially pleased that many of our students have chosen to continue their journey with us in Sixth Form.
Today marks the beginning of an exciting new chapter, and we look forward to welcoming them back in September as they begin Year 12 and take the next steps towards their ambitions.
Mr Alec Waters, Headteacher, said: "Today has been a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the achievements of our students alongside their families. Their resilience, dedication and positive attitude throughout their studies have been outstanding, and we are incredibly proud of everything they have accomplished. We are delighted that so many students will be continuing their education with us in Sixth Form, and we look forward to seeing them thrive in Year 12 from September."
Miss Kate Mowatt, Head of Year 11, said: "I am incredibly proud of our students and all they have achieved. They have worked hard throughout their GCSEs, and today’s results show that their efforts have paid off. It has been a pleasure to support them on their journey, and I cannot wait to see what they go on to achieve next."
We'd like to congratulate all of our students on their GCSE results today. We wish them every success for the future and look forward to celebrating many more achievements with them in the years ahead.
Our co-educational Sixth Form welcomes applications from all students. We've created an environment that supports academic growth, personal development and a smooth transition from GCSEs to the exciting opportunities that lie beyond school. If you're interested in joining Ribston's Sixth Form, please email our Sixth Form team: sixthform@ribstonhall.gloucs.sch.uk.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ribston Hall High School - Ribston Hall High School Celebrates Outstanding GCSE and A 'Level Success
pageCache.text:
Ribston Hall High School Celebrates Outstanding GCSE and A 'Level Success
Ribston Hall High School is celebrating exceptional examination results across both A Levels and GCSEs, marking one of the most successful years in recent memory.
Over 50% of students achieved grades A*- B in their A 'Levels and many subjects saw a significant rise in top grades. STEM subjects have been a real strength this year. In GCSE Biology, Chemistry, and Physics we saw double the percentage of grade 9s compared with last year, while Maths recorded a 17% increase in top grades. This success reflects the investment in our STEM curriculum and the state-of-the-art science facilities that were opened in 2022.
Exceptional Achievements
Most of our students secured places at their first-choice universities, including Bristol (Physics, Maths, Engineering, Medical Microbiology, Biochemistry, Psychology), Birmingham (Law, Neuroscience), Cardiff (Pharmacy, Radiotherapy, Physics), Sheffield (History), Bath (History), Plymouth (History), and Aberdeen (Neuroscience), with others having secured apprenticeships in subjects ranging from Finance to Cybersecurity.
GCSE's results marked a decade high (excluding Covid years) with one-third of results awarded at grades 8 & 9 and over 50% receiving top grades 9-7.
“We are delighted to share this year’s GCSE and A Level results. Our students’ academic achievements are outstanding, but their success goes far beyond the exams. It has been a pleasure to watch them grow, and through their hard work, alongside the support of our dedicated staff, achieve such exceptional grades. Every one of these students has made a hugely positive contribution to school life at Ribston, and we are immensely proud of their achievements.” Mr. Alec Waters, Headteacher
“I am incredibly proud of our students’ achievements this year and excited to see the opportunities ahead for them, with outstanding A ‘Level results and excellent EPQ outcomes. The majority of this cohort also completed their Ribston Baccalaureate, a unique programme that enhances skills and supports both academic excellence and holistic development, ensuring students are equipped to thrive at university and in the workplace. These achievements have strengthened applications to some of the UK’s top universities.” Sixth Form Lead, Mrs. Cat Nicklin
Pride in Our School Community
These excellent results are a testament not only to the hard work and determination of our students, but also to the dedication of our staff, the support of our families, and the culture of praise and recognition we foster at Ribston Hall. We encourage our students to challenge themselves, grow in confidence, and celebrate success in all its forms. These outcomes showcase the strength of our school community, and we remain committed to ensuring that every student feels recognised and celebrated for their achievements, both within and beyond the classroom.
Congratulations once again to all our students — we are so proud of everything you have accomplished.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ribston Hall High School - Rosalind Franklin Science Centre
pageCache.text:
Rosalind Franklin Science Centre
The Rosalind Franklin Science Centre was opened in May 2022 to strengthen our STEM offering with six cutting-edge labs, as well as prep rooms and offices. Scientist Dr Caitlin Higgott, of the Rosalind Franklin Institute in Oxford, formally opened the facility.
Delivering a first-class learning environment for students and staff, the science facility comprises six science labs, two preparation rooms and further offices, helping us to truly cement ourselves as a STEM centre of excellence. An array of rooftop photovoltaic solar panels is generating electricity to help power energy-efficient lighting and heating systems within the ‘Franklin’ building.
Students were asked to nominate inspirational scientists to name the facility and a school-wide vote led to the centre being named in recognition of one of the unsung heroes of 20th century Science, Chemist Rosalind Franklin.
Half-way point - October 2021
The window frames are now in place and the glazing is expected to be fitted by the end of the month, making the building watertight at the half-way point of 22 weeks into our 44 week build. We can see the teaching space taking shape now as internal walls have been constructed.
We are about to launch the final voting round of a competition to name the new Science Building, with some excellent suggestions of female British scientists having been put forward by students.
Autumn progress - September 2021
The cladding is now largely in place and the building should be watertight next month. It's great to see the new science facility looking so advanced and for us to see the new Ribston Hall landscape unfold.
Summer progress - July/August 2021
We can now see the final form of the building, enabling us to visualise how it will sit within the school landscape. We can't wait for our budding scientists to use this cutting edge facility next Spring.
Building progress - June 2021
The foundations are now laid for our new science centre, with the first upright steels being fitted this month. It was a grey day outside, but not for us here as we watched a milestone moment in the build unfolding.
Architectural imagery - May 2021
We're pleased to be able to share with you some new imagery of how our new science centre will look once it's completed next Spring. We broke ground for the new building in the middle of May.
Planning Permission granted – November 2020
Ribston Hall High School was granted planning permission by Gloucester City Council to build a new science block to provide state-of-the-art facilities for use by all of our young scientists. This new stand alone accessible building will be situated on the south side of the school site and will provide accommodation for six laboratories, including two spacious prep rooms and office space.

At Ribston, we are proud to offer a wide range of educational visits, residential experiences and enrichment opportunities that enhance learning beyond the classroom and help students develop confidence, independence and new interests.
The school offers many extra-curricular activities. These give pupils a chance to explore talents and interests in sports, the arts, culture, volunteering and leadership...Disadvantaged pupils and those with special educational needs and/or disabilities participate fully in these experiences.
Whilst we understand that families may wish to plan ahead, it is unfortunately not possible for us to provide a complete schedule of trips and visits for the academic year. Alongside a small number of established annual events, many opportunities arise throughout the year in response to educational experiences such as theatre productions, exhibitions, competitions, university events and subject-specific opportunities.

School Trips and Educational Visits
School trips and educational visits give our students the chance to take their learning beyond the classroom and experience new things. Our trips and visits build confidence, curiosity and independence, while strengthening teamwork and social skills.
Whether exploring museums, visiting outdoor spaces or cultural landmarks, our students gain a deeper understanding of the world around them and create memorable experiences that enrich their personal growth and academic progress.
There are many opportunities for trips and visits throughout your child's career at Ribston, including ski trips and sports tours. pageCache.text:
Ribston Hall High School Celebrates Positive Ofsted Report Under New National Framework
Ribston is delighted to share the outcome of its recent Ofsted inspection, which took place in May 2026. The final report provides a highly positive reflection of our school, recognising the strength of its culture, the quality of education provided, and the exceptional outcomes achieved by students.
Inspectors highlighted a number of defining features that make Ribston such a special place to learn and grow. The report praises pupils who “excel across the curriculum” and consistently achieve academically above national averages. It also recognises the school's culture of “kindness and respect”, where exemplary behaviour and high attendance contribute to a positive and purposeful learning environment.
The inspection team commended Ribston's ambitious and carefully planned curriculum, which challenges and supports learners of all abilities. Teaching was recognised as highly effective, underpinned by strong subject expertise and a shared commitment to academic excellence. Inspectors also celebrated the school's extensive personal development provision, including the Ribston Baccalaureate and Ambition Pathway, which help students develop the skills, confidence and experiences needed for future success.
At the heart of the report is recognition of the school's students. Inspectors describe Ribston pupils as confident, articulate and intellectually curious young people who embrace challenge, support one another and make meaningful contributions to school life. These qualities reflect the values that underpin the Ribston experience: developing ambitious academic learners, confident and creative thinkers, and students who are proud to belong to the school community.
The inspection was conducted under Ofsted's revised framework, which introduces a broader range of judgements and raises expectations across all areas of school provision. The framework also includes an additional judgement of "Exceptional", above the previous Outstanding grade, making it one of the most demanding inspection models introduced to date.
Within this context, Ribston was judged to meet or exceed the expected standard across all areas, with the majority of provision recognised as being at a strong standard. Importantly, the expected standard represents a high national benchmark and reflects rigorous professional and statutory expectations across the education sector.
As part of the inspection process, areas for further development were also identified. These focus on strengthening the precision of evaluating impact, particularly in relation to SEND provision and aspects of post-16 oversight. These priorities align closely with areas already identified within the school's own self-evaluation and will help shape the next stage of its improvement journey.
Reflecting on the outcome, our leadership team described the report as a celebration of the collective efforts of students, staff, parents and trustees, and a testament to the strength of the Ribston community.
The report paints a picture of a purposeful, ambitious and inclusive school where students thrive both academically and personally. It reflects a community in which young people feel safe, valued and inspired to achieve their best, while remaining rooted in the values of kindness, respect and ambition.
Ribston would like to thank all members of its community for the role they have played in this success. The strong partnership between home and school continues to be one of Ribston's greatest strengths, and the school looks forward to building on this positive outcome as it continues its journey of excellence.
You can download our full Ofsted Report on the Ofsted website.
Alec Waters, Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Ribston Hall High School - Ribston Students Join International Model UN
pageCache.text:
Ribston Students Join International Model UN
Students across Years 9, 11, 12 and 13 met with schools from across the world to take part in Model UN this month.
Model UN is an educational simulation of the United Nations, where students represent different countries, research global issues and debate resolutions in a formal setting, just as delegates do at real UN conferences.
33 Ribston students were part of the International Model UN project. Ribston, along with 13 other schools from China, Kenya and the UK, each represented a country and took part in debates to try and pass the resolutions set by the “real” UN during last year’s COP29 talks.
In the three weeks leading up to the event, students met regularly to research the country they were representing — Mauritius — and to understand how climate change is affecting the country in terms of deforestation, plastic pollution, sustainability in fashion, carbon production and financing adaptations. They explored Mauritius’ economic position, environmental vulnerabilities and political priorities in order to represent the country accurately and responsibly.
The day itself required students to think quickly, listen carefully and respond thoughtfully as debates developed. They used a variety of skills including teamwork, leadership, public speaking, empathy and critical thinking, working collaboratively to negotiate, challenge and support proposed resolutions.
We were so proud of the way they conducted themselves in the debating sessions and gained the confidence to argue points that would not necessarily be beneficial to Mauritius, but reflected the complex realities of international politics.
We hope they now have a better understanding of global issues and the challenges of reaching agreement on matters that affect countries in very different ways.
Well done to all our Ribston students who took part. We are incredibly proud of them — our future leaders in the making!
